name: St. Peter's Basilica
overview: St. Peter's Basilica is one of the largest churches in the world and a masterpiece of Renaissance architecture. Located in Vatican City, it's built over the burial site of Saint Peter and is the principal church of the Catholic Church.
history: This sacred site marks where Saint Peter, the first Pope and Jesus's apostle, was crucified upside down by Emperor Nero in 64 AD. Emperor Constantine built the first basilica here in 326 AD over Peter's tomb. The current Renaissance masterpiece took 120 years to complete (1506-1626), with legendary artists Bramante, Michelangelo, Maderno, and Bernini each contributing their genius. Michelangelo designed the iconic dome at age 71, working without payment as his service to God. This is where Popes are crowned, where pilgrims from around the world come to pray, and where some of humanity's greatest artistic treasures reside. The basilica has witnessed countless historic moments, from papal conclaves to the funeral of Pope John Paul II attended by world leaders.
highlights: Michelangelo's Pietà - his only signed sculpture
Bernini's Baldachin - massive bronze canopy over the altar
Climb the dome designed by Michelangelo for panoramic views
St. Peter's tomb beneath the main altar
tips: Entry to the basilica is free, but dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees). Dome climb requires separate ticket and involves 551 steps. Visit early morning or late afternoon to avoid crowds. Security lines can be long, so arrive early.
